text:
marco: Heads-up: encountered intermittent SSL verification errors only when using the AsyncClient on Windows + py3.10 in our onboarding tests. Sync client works fine.

anya: Can you paste the minimal repro? We want to add it to the CI matrix if it's flaky.

marco: Sure. Steps: create venv on Windows, pip install redwood-sdk (0.9.2), httpx[http2], certifi, then run this script.

```python
# async_repro.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-test")
    await c.chat.create(model="gptx-mini", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}])

asyncio.run(main())
```

marco: Error: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate.

anya: Quick check: does setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() make it go away?

marco: Yes, setting SSL_CERT_FILE to the certifi bundle resolves it. But that's not ideal because customers expect the SDK to use the platform store on Windows (internal CAs are common).

dave: This sounds like cafile precedence: if you create SSLContext with cafile explicitly, OpenSSL will ignore the Windows cert store. We might be passing cafile unconditionally for deterministic certs in hosted envs.

anya: Which path only affects async? Maybe the sync transport uses requests/urllib3 which defers to platform certs, while async uses httpx/anyio which we configure differently.

marco: Exactly. Repro shows sync client fine, async fails. I inspected our wheel and found code in redwood/transport/async_http.py constructing SSLContext with cafile=certifi.where().

dave: Proposed quick fixes: (1) on Windows, prefer create_default_context() without cafile unless env vars SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR are set; (2) add AsyncClient param `use_system_certs` defaulting to None so we can flip behavior via config; (3) document Windows troubleshooting in the SDK docs.

anya: I support adding the param for customers needing explicit control. Also add a short troubleshooting snippet in quickstart and the Windows compatibility doc.

marco: Can we add an integration test matrix entry for windows-py310 and windows-py311 that runs a basic async request (mocked endpoint) to validate we don't regress this?

triage-bot: created ticket SDK-8792: "Windows async: cert store precedence leading to SSLCertVerificationError" with labels: devex, windows, py3.10, py3.11, sdk.

dave: I'll open PR fix/win-async-cert-precedence-8792. Plan: change async transport to call ssl.create_default_context() on Windows unless env is set, add `use_system_certs` param, add unit test asserting context options, and add docs blurb. Will add changelog entry for 0.9.3.

anya: For release notes mention: "Windows: AsyncClient respects system certificate store by default to avoid verification failures with internal CAs (opt-in flag provided for backward compatibility)."

marco: One more ask: add a short paragraph to the onboarding checklist that tells support engineers to try SSL_CERT_FILE workaround and to suggest `use_system_certs=True` once the patch ships. Saves time in support loops.

triage-bot: CI pipeline triggered for branch fix/win-async-cert-precedence-8792 — windows-py310, windows-py311, linux-py311.

anya: Thanks team. Follow-up: once PR is merged let's push a patch (0.9.3) and notify CS so they can update onboarding docs and customer templates.
